steps.title: Prepare 1% agarose gel
steps.instruction: Mix 1 g agarose powder, 2 mL 50× TAE stock (to 1× final), and 98 mL Milli‑Q water per 100 mL; heat to 75‑80 °C until dissolved, cool to ~45 °C and add 2 µL ethidium bromide (100 mg/mL stock), then let solidify at 22‑25 °C. Use 1× TAE (Thermo Scientific Cat# B49) as running buffer.

steps.title: Prepare LB medium with kanamycin
steps.instruction: Weigh 2.0 g LB powder, dissolve in 100 mL distilled water, aliquot 10 mL into each sterile glass tube (Borosil Cat# 9820U08), seal with cotton plugs, autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min (15 psi). After cooling to ~45 °C, add 10 µL kanamycin (HiMedia). Store tubes at 4 °C and use within 2 weeks.

steps.title: Surface‑sterilize and imbibe seeds
steps.instruction: Surface‑sterilize jute seeds (method not detailed) and place them in sterile water for overnight imbibition.

steps.title: Pierce imbibed seeds
steps.instruction: Flame‑sterilize a needle, allow it to cool, and pierce each imbibed seed near the apical meristematic zone of the plumule; each seed may be pierced a maximum of two times.

steps.title: Soak seeds in infiltration medium
steps.instruction: Prepare infiltration and co‑cultivation medium containing Agrobacterium tumefaciens at OD 0.3 and acetosyringone (add before seed immersion, mix by pipetting 10‑20 times). Submerge pierced seeds, cover with aluminum foil, and incubate 30 min–1 h at 22‑25 °C with gentle agitation. Use 25 mL medium for a 100 mm plate (Corning Cat# BP94A‑01) or 6 mL for a 35 mm plate (Tarsons Cat# 460035‑35MM).

steps.title: Vacuum infiltrate seeds
steps.instruction: Clean a vacuum desiccator with 70 % ethanol and expose to UV light for 30 min under laminar flow. Place the petri plates with submerged seeds inside and apply vacuum for 10 min at 550 mm Hg (do not exceed 20 min).

steps.title: Blot excess Agrobacterium
steps.instruction: Transfer seeds onto sterile Whatman No. 1 filter paper (or sterile blotting paper) and incubate 5 min to remove excess liquid.

steps.title: Initiate co‑cultivation
steps.instruction: Move seeds to a 100 mm petri plate containing Whatman No. 1 filter paper, add 3 mL co‑cultivation medium (same composition as step 5 but without Agrobacterium), seal with Parafilm, cover with aluminum foil, and incubate 72 h at 28 °C in the dark. Ensure media volume is adequate – not excessive (prevents browning) nor scarce (prevents drying).

steps.title: Wash seeds post‑co‑cultivation
steps.instruction: Transfer seeds to a fresh 100 mm petri plate and wash four times, each wash lasting 5 min, using Agro‑washing medium without any antibiotic (sterile water can be used but medium gives better results).

steps.title: Antibiotic treatment and second vacuum
steps.instruction: Submerge seeds in Agro‑washing medium containing timentin (HiMedia Cat# PCT1113‑2G) or 1 g/L cefotaxime (HiMedia Cat# MB134) for 20 min, then vacuum infiltrate for 5 min at 550 mm Hg.

steps.title: Dry seeds before selection
steps.instruction: Place seeds on sterile Whatman No. 1 filter paper and incubate 45 min to achieve a semi‑dry state.

steps.title: First hygromycin selection
steps.instruction: Transfer seeds to round screw‑cap phyta jars (HiMedia Cat# PW1125) containing selection medium with hygromycin‑B (15 mg/L for JRC212 seeds, 18 mg/L for JRO524 seeds). Prepare selection medium freshly and add hygromycin after autoclaved media cool to ~45 °C (before solidification). Incubate 14 days at 27 ± 2 °C with a photoperiod of 16 h light / 8 h dark.

steps.title: Second hygromycin selection
steps.instruction: Transfer surviving seedlings to fresh selection medium (same hygromycin concentration) and grow for another 14 days under identical conditions. Place five to six plants per magenta box (HiMedia Cat# PW1138).

steps.title: Third hygromycin selection (optional)
steps.instruction: Transfer seedlings to fresh selection medium for a third 14‑day round under the same temperature and photoperiod. This step maximizes transformed plant recovery but may be omitted if time‑constrained.

steps.title: Hygromycin‑free growth (optional)
steps.instruction: Grow the selected plants for 10 days in medium lacking hygromycin‑B to promote root development.

steps.title: Root cleaning and transplantation
steps.instruction: Rinse plant roots thoroughly with sterile water, taking care not to damage them, and transplant the seedlings into soil in the greenhouse. Avoid leaving media residues on roots to prevent fungal contamination.

steps.title: Genomic DNA isolation from leaves
steps.instruction: Collect fully opened young leaves from each plant, wash twice with ddH₂O and blot dry. Use the Macherey‑Nagel plant DNA isolation kit (Cat# 740770) following the manufacturer’s protocol. Measure DNA concentration with a Thermo Scientific NanoDrop 2000C spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Calculate transformation efficiency
steps.instruction: Determine efficiency as (Number of PCR‑positive plants ÷ Total number of imbibed seeds) × 100. Compute mean efficiency across three independent experiments using Microsoft Excel.

description: Jute holds immense potential as a global bast fiber crop. However, limited genetic engineering research presents bottleneck conditions in jute improvement for diversified applications. This opens exciting avenues for them who have an easy, efficient, reliable, and reproducible transformation protocol. Agrobacterium-mediated transformation (AMT) protocols are more commonly used in jute than any other method of plant transformation protocols.2 Currently, the shoot tip (explant) method of Agrobacterium-mediated transformation in jute is used for transgenic jute development.3,4,5,6,7 Time duration, tissue culture dependency for regeneration of the shoot tip to a plant, and transformation efficiency are the limitations of the current shoot tip method, despite it being a stable and efficient method. Overcoming these limitations, here we present an improved plant genetic transformation protocol for jute that is easy, reliable, reproducible, less time-consuming in explant preparation, with fewer media and resource requirements, partial dependency on tissue culture, and facilitating a higher transformation efficiency. This protocol is known as the imbibed seed piercing method (ISPM) for AMT in jute and offers a foundation for stable and successful jute crop improvement, fulfilling the high demand for strong, long, and environment friendly fibers. Overall, in the ISPM for AMT protocol, jute seeds are subjected to surface sterilization, followed by overnight imbibition in water and piercing with a needle to facilitate the penetration of Agrobacterium cell suspension through vacuum infiltration. Transformed jute seeds are selected by growing them in a medium supplemented with hygromycin-B. The transgene integration is confirmed through PCR analysis. PCR-based plant genotyping minimizes the risk of selecting false-positive plants during the antibiotic-based selection of transformants.
